raw_case_text:
Our 61-year-old male patient initially presented in 2018 with a mass on the lower right side of his neck. A core needle biopsy revealed monophasic synovial sarcoma, t(X;18)(p11;q11). Staging scans did not show distant metastases. He received 2 cycles of doxorubicin and ifosfamide (AIM) chemotherapy, followed by 60 Gy of radiation therapy to the neck, and 2 additional cycles of AIM. He developed biopsy-proven lung metastasis 6 months after completing chemotherapy. He was treated with pazopanib and pembrolizumab without response. Pazopanib is a potent oral multi-target inhibitor against receptor tyrosine kinases including VEGFR-1, -2, and -3, PDGFR, and c-Kit. Pembrolizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody directed against the checkpoint protein, programmed cell death-1, which stimulates the immune system's response against tumor cells.
He subsequently transferred care to our institution in February 2021 and enrolled in the phase 2 clinical trial of afami-cel (SPEARHEAD-1; NCT04044768). HLAx02 and MAGE-A4 positive participants in this trial undergo leukapheresis, and their isolated T-cells are transduced with the MAGE-A4 T-cell receptor and expanded (Fig. 2).
Our patient underwent apheresis in March 2021. Lymphodepletion with fludarabine 20 mg/m2 (planned reduction from 30 mg/m2 per protocol due to renal function) and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 and T-cell infusion with a dose of 4,893.4 x 106 transduced cells occurred in May 2021. Acyclovir treatment was initiated at the time of infusion at a dose of 800 mg twice daily.
The patient experienced grade 2 cytokine release syndrome (CRS) on day +2 and grade 1 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome and required treatment with tocilizumab and dexamethasone, oxygen for transient hypoxia, and iv saline bolus for hypotension. Tocilizumab is a humanized mouse monoclonal antibody that is designed to bind both mIL-6R (membrane bound receptor for IL-6 and sIL-6R [soluble receptor for IL-6]) and can inhibit both classical and trans-signaling pathway to treat cytokine storm. These adverse events were resolved by day +8.
The patient experienced prolonged cytopenias which manifested initially as grade 3 neutropenia on day +2 with further multiple neutropenia occurrences with final resolution on day +63. The worst grade experienced was grade 4 lasting 4 days, and patient required granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support.
The patient achieved a confirmed partial response per RECIST 1.1. on study with maximum reduction in target lesions of 67.6% at week 24 following infusion. Interestingly, routine surveillance PET/CT in October 2021 showed new intensely hypermetabolic bilateral adrenal masses. Biopsy of right adrenal gland showed a polymorphic LPD, EBV-positive, suspected to be secondary to treatment-related immunodeficiency. Next-generation sequencing by Heme Stanford Actionable Mutation Panel for Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Malignancies (Heme-STAMP) showed a variant of unknown significance (SOCS1 S143_F144insYGSRES), which does not lend support for recurrent genetic alterations found in hematolymphoid neoplasms. Note that there was no reported target or non-target lesion in the adrenal gland at baseline.
In December 2021, he was treated with 2 cycles of trabectedin for disease progression of sarcoma which were complicated by rhabdomyolysis, CMV reactivation, and non ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Trabectedin is an alkylating agent that binds guanine residues in the minor groove of DNA, which interferes with genetic transcription processes and induces lethal single-strand and double-strand DNA breaks. Trabectedin was discontinued in February 2022. Imaging showed favorable response to pulmonary and pleural lesions after treatment with trabectedin.
For the new diagnosis of secondary EBV LPD, he completed 4 weekly doses of rituximab 375 mg/m2 in April 2022. PET scan in June showed resolution of lymphoproliferative disease to treatment with metabolic resolution of the right adrenal lesion and decreased size and metabolic uptake of the left adrenal lesion (Fig. 3). Scan also showed interval disease progression off therapy while recovering from trabectedin toxicity with growing pleural and pulmonary nodules, and new hypermetabolic right cervical lymph node.
On study entry, the patient was CMV IgG and EBV IgG positive (IgM negative). Peak CMV was 2002 IU/ML in January 2022 and peak EBV 3450 in March 2022. In April, following initiation of rituxan CMV and EBV were undetectable and in June 2022 there was undetectable CMV and low positivity EBV, and the LPD event was considered resolved.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 61-year-old male with metastatic synovial sarcoma underwent MAGE-A4 TCR-engineered T-cell therapy (afami-cel) and subsequently developed bilateral adrenal masses and treatment-related complications.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Originally diagnosed in 2018 with right lower neck monophasic synovial sarcoma t(X;18)(p11;q11), the patient developed biopsy-proven lung metastases 6 months after surgery/cheoradiation (4 cycles AIM + 60 Gy RT) and progressed through pazopanib and pembrolizumab. He enrolled in the SPEARHEAD-1 phase 2 trial of afami-cel, undergoing leukapheresis in March 2021 and lymphodepletion (fludarabine 20 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2) followed by infusion of 4,893.4 x 10^6 transduced MAGE-A4 TCR T-cells in May 2021 (with acyclovir 800 mg BID prophylaxis). Early post-infusion course was complicated by grade 2 CRS and grade 1 ICANS on day +2 (resolved by day +8 with tocilizumab, dexamethasone, oxygen, and IV fluids) and recurrent grade 3-4 neutropenia resolving on day +63 with G-CSF. He achieved a 67.6% partial response of sarcoma target lesions at week 24, but October 2021 surveillance PET/CT identified new intensely hypermetabolic bilateral adrenal masses, and December 2021 salvage trabectedin for sarcoma progression was complicated by rhabdomyolysis, CMV reactivation, and NSTEMI.
subjective.past_medical_history: Metastatic monophasic synovial sarcoma t(X;18)(p11;q11) (HLA*A02 and MAGE-A4 positive) status post AIM chemotherapy, neck radiation (60 Gy), pazopanib, pembrolizumab, and afami-cel TCR T-cell therapy (May 2021); baseline renal impairment requiring fludarabine dose reduction; baseline CMV IgG+ and EBV IgG+ (IgM-).
subjective.review_of_systems: Post-afami-cel transient hypoxia and hypotension during CRS (day +2 to +8); asymptomatic discovery of bilateral adrenal masses on surveillance PET/CT (October 2021); subsequent rhabdomyolysis and NSTEMI during trabectedin therapy (December 2021).

objective.physical_examination: Transient hypoxia and hypotension on day +2 post-afami-cel infusion during grade 2 CRS and grade 1 ICANS (resolved by day +8).
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline CMV IgG positive, EBV IgG positive, IgM negative. Post-infusion grade 3-4 neutropenia from day +2 to day +63. During trabectedin therapy (Dec 2021 - Mar 2022): laboratory evidence of rhabdomyolysis, NSTEMI, peak plasma CMV viral load of 2,002 IU/mL in January 2022, and peak EBV viral load of 3,450 IU/mL in March 2022.
objective.advanced_workup: October 2021 surveillance FDG PET/CT showed 67.6% reduction in target sarcoma lesions (RECIST 1.1 partial response) but revealed new intensely hypermetabolic bilateral adrenal masses. Right adrenal gland biopsy demonstrated EBV-positive polymorphic lymphoproliferative disorder (LPD) secondary to treatment-related immunodeficiency; Heme-STAMP NGS showed only a SOCS1 S143_F144insYGSRES variant of unknown significance. Follow-up PET/CT in June 2022 after rituximab showed complete metabolic resolution of the right adrenal lesion and decreased size/uptake of the left adrenal lesion, alongside progression of pleural/pulmonary sarcoma nodules and a new hypermetabolic right cervical lymph node.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with secondary EBV-positive polymorphic lymphoproliferative disorder (LPD) of the bilateral adrenal glands (confirmed by right adrenal biopsy and peak EBV load 3,450 IU/mL) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation (confirmed by peak plasma CMV viral load 2,002 IU/mL in January 2022) following afami-cel TCR T-cell therapy and trabectedin chemotherapy for metastatic synovial sarcoma. Trabectedin was discontinued in February 2022 after 2 cycles due to rhabdomyolysis, NSTEMI, and CMV reactivation. Completed 4 weekly infusions of rituximab (375 mg/m2) in April 2022, achieving undetectable CMV viral load, near-clearance of EBV viremia, and resolution of adrenal EBV-LPD on June 2022 PET/CT.
